chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: Head arrangements and the Hi-Q publishing credit
summary: Heads arose from riffs set by section leaders.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You know, when anybody sat in like that, you'd do mostly head arrangements.

Uh-huh. Speaking of head arrangements, noticed in some of the recordings that the things that has Earl's name as composer, and there's no arranger credit given, I presume those were mostly heads. But they're published by a company called Hi-Q Productions. Which is like the first two letters of Hines' name. Were you the "Q"? C-u-e.
I don't know. Could have been.
Well, it sounds like a company, so I don't know what it was, but how did the head arrangements come about at the Terrace? Was it behind the shows or spin-offs of stocks, or what?
Well, a head arrangement came about just by musicians knowing the different tunes.
Uh-huh. And would the section leader set a riff, or --
Yeah, section leader set the riff.
And this would sort of evolve into a set routine?
Did the Hines band have a lot of head arrangements?
We didn't have too many. We didn't have too many.
